extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of newspaper journalism / sports reporters and editors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing newspaper sports coverage, including pre-game previews, game-day features, play-by-play reports, and post-game analysis, with attention to purpose, treatment, style, and necessary factual elements (lineups, officials, stats).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of sporting news stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Sporting news stories may be divided into three classes: (1) those that deal with the contestants and the conditions before the event, (2) those that report the contest itself, and (3) those that analyze the event and its results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories discussing contestants and forecasts should be based on first-hand observations or others' observations of past showings and practice. Detailed accounts of a contest require writers who witnessed it. Analysis may be based on the reporter's observation or on printed reports. For big events, assign two reporters: one for a general account and one for a detailed play-by-play.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of sports reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The general aim of sporting news stories should be to satisfy a normal, healthy interest in legitimate sports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid stimulating excessive interest in professional or college athletics that can have harmful effects on athletes. Maintain accuracy and fairness as vitally as in other news stories; local interest doesn't justify slighting opponents. Consider educators' criticisms about undue publicity and its effects on schoolboy and college athletes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment — review and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews of conditions preceding the contest and analyses of the game and its results require careful observation, clear thinking, and a good expository style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This kind of interpretation is in some respects not unlike editorial and critical writing; it should explain causes, evaluate performances, and put the contest in larger context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment — account of the event
rubrics_metrics.description: The account of the event itself demands spirited narrative and description that portrays not only the scenes but the spirit of the occasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contrasts (victors vs. vanquished), develop personal or human-interest elements (players as 'heroes'), and convey the atmosphere and emotion of the contest. The narrative should be vivid and engaging rather than merely clinical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style and variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of heavy, repetitive subject matter, sports writing needs variety of presentation and readable style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid constant repetition; resist cheap humor and unintelligible jargon. Strive for picturesque diction and original figures of speech where appropriate, but ensure good English and clarity. Readable, original sports stories in proper English are preferable to jargon or forced 'cleverness.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Most papers have a special staff of sports writers under the direction of the sporting editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sporting news stories can best be written by reporters who are thoroughly familiar with the sport and the contestants. Use specialized beats and editors to provide consistent, knowledgeable coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-game (prospect) coverage elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-contest stories should deal with contestants and conditions before the event: injuries, likely absences, practice reports, probable lineups, and team morale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include coach comments, how replacements may affect team strength, conditioning notes, travel and lodging arrangements for teams, and the stakes of the game (implications for future opponents). Provide enough context so readers understand significance and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Day-of-game / feature description
rubrics_metrics.description: Game-day features should capture setting and atmosphere: weather, crowd, traditions, pageantry, travel of fans, and any local color or legal/regulatory quirks affecting spectators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sensory detail (sight, sound, smell), describe processions, alumni reunions, banners/flags (including restrictions), and stadium conditions to set the scene and increase reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Game report and play-by-play structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed game reports should present a play-by-play or detailed account, and include standard factual blocks such as lineups, officials, time of periods, and start time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the detailed play-by-play under a separate heading from the general account. Provide an initial lineup block (players, positions, substitutes), list officials by name and affiliation, and state game start time and period lengths. Use clear chronology in the play-by-play and separate scoring sequences for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-game analysis and statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-game analysis should examine tactics, comparative strengths and weaknesses, and relevant statistics (rushing yards, first downs, forward-pass gains, punts, penalties, fumbles, substitutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use statistics to support judgments (e.g., 'Yale gained 298 yards by rushing to Princeton's 145'). Discuss how tactics (line plunges, forward passes, punting strategy) affected the outcome; assess individual performances and the impact of substitutes. Report penalties, turnovers, and other decisive factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness and balance in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy and fairness are as vital to news stories of sports as to any other news stories; the spirit of fair play is necessary in reports of sporting events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when local readers prefer one side, do not slight opponents. Present balanced treatment of both teams and avoid partisan exaggeration. Strive for impartial tone, correct attribution of quotes and actions, and equitable attention to notable individual play on both sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-interest and characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of popular interest in individual players, many events give ample opportunity for developing personal or human-interest elements; athletes are often portrayed as 'heroes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use anecdotes, descriptions of emotions, injuries, recoveries, and small personal details to humanize players and connect readers to the story, while not sacrificing factual accuracy or fairness.
